t: A Weser port that won self-government from its archbishops after Frederick Barbarossa's privilege of 1186.
A Hanseatic city and free imperial city, it resisted Swedish claims and survived the end of the Holy Roman Empire in 1806.
Through Bremerhaven it became a great emigration port, and it is now the smallest state of the Federal Republic of Germany.
dyk: The Ratskeller wine cellar beneath Bremen's town hall, in use since the early fifteenth century, still keeps a cask of Rüdesheim wine from 1653.
ev: Frederick Barbarossa's Gelnhausen Privilege confirms the citizens' rights
The stone Roland statue is set up in the market square
The Linz Diploma confirms Bremen as a free imperial city
Johann Smidt founds Bremerhaven at the mouth of the Weser
Norddeutscher Lloyd is founded in Bremen
The Land of Bremen is re-established with Bremerhaven
Bremen becomes a state of the Federal Republic of Germany

f.founder: Citizens of Bremen (privilege of Frederick Barbarossa, 1186)
